00 Overview

EMRC Showroom OS · Design System

Visual identity for the LUT EMRC visitor showroom. Nine 4K touchpoints, eight landscape and one portrait, telling the energy-transition story to politicians, funders and students. Cinematic, editorial, technical — closer to a Bloomberg terminal than a consumer app.

Surface
#161c26
Deep navy-charcoal, warm enough to read as ink, not void.
Spine
Electric ↔ Legacy
Future vs past. The single semantic axis.
Type
DIN Pro Medium
One family, one weight. Hierarchy via size + tracking.
Grid
3840 × 2160
Native resolution. Every value is literal Figma pixels.
Reach
Bottom third
All controls in the bottom third of landscape touchpoints.
Codes
Battle · Doc · Cinema · Builder
One storytelling code per frame. Never mix.

What this document is

The single source of truth for design across all EMRC Showroom touchpoints. Tokens, components and rules — surfaced here as a living, interactive reference. Every component on this page renders at native 4K pixel dimensions inside a viewport-scaled card, so what you see preserves the real proportions a touchpoint would render.

Authority: this page reflects the design system encoded in DESIGN.md (the lintable token contract) and operationalised by EMRC-design.md (workflow, editorial, touchpoint specifics). The Figma file (3ewb83nlq9PyBOrpzYHiax) remains authoritative for any pixel value not encoded here.

How to read this

FOUNDATIONS
Color · Type · Spacing · Radii · Elevation · Layout. The tokens every component consumes.
COMPONENTS
Twelve interactive component cards. State toggles are live. Each card carries specs + Do/Don't.
PATTERNS + RULES
Four storytelling codes. Two-register architecture. The running anti-patterns list — keep adding to it.

The constitutional rule

§1 · Rendering principle
All touchpoints render at native Figma 4K resolution and scale via CSS transform to fit the viewport. One source of truth. No conversion math.
#stage { width: 3840px; height: 2160px; transform: scale(var(--scale)); }
F.01 Foundations

Color is semantic, never decorative.

The palette has three groups. The brand spine (Electric / Legacy) carries the EMRC argument across every touchpoint. Page chrome is the canvas it lives on. Test Outcome accents appear only inside Test Outcome components — using them anywhere else dilutes their signal.

Brand spine

Electric is the future tense. Legacy is the past tense. They are never reversed — Electric is always LEFT, Legacy always RIGHT, in every comparative composition.

Electric
#787AFFFuture, electricity, primary CTAs
Legacy
#E87975Past, fossil fuels, thermal engines
Off-White
#F1F3FCDefault text & surface
Black
#000000Action Bar (Black), Source Drawer (Viewing)

Page chrome

Environmental tokens applied to layout wrappers and body backgrounds — not to individual components. Surface is the default; Panel-Deep is reserved for Cover frames and dense data side-panels.

Surface
#161C26Default body background
Panel
#0E131CInset cards, recessed panels
Panel Deep
#0A0E14Cover frame, side data panels

Test outcome accents

Use only inside Test Outcome and Test Outcome Comment. Color is the signal — using these tokens decoratively makes a real "negative" reading indistinguishable from a styling choice.

Positive
#4ADE80Test Outcome — beats target
Average
#DEC04ATest Outcome — on target
Negative
#E74747Test Outcome — misses target

Translucent overlays

The system Selected pattern is backdrop-blur(20px) +rgba(241, 243, 252, 0.2) + 1px rgba(241, 243, 252, 0.3) border. Used by Selector, Tertiary (Tapped), Source Drawer (Open). Text stays Off-White — the color never inverts.

Do

  • Use Electric for every reference to electricity and every primary CTA.
  • Use Legacy exclusively for fossil fuels and thermal engines.
  • Apply the Selected pattern consistently across Selector / Tertiary Tapped / Source Drawer Open.
  • Place chrome (Header, Bottom Nav, Source Drawer Badge) at z-index ≥ 10 — content backgrounds otherwise cover them.

Don't

  • Don't reverse spatial grammar — Electric on the right or Legacy on the left.
  • Don't introduce new accent colors. Test Outcome tokens never appear outside Test Outcome.
  • Don't invert (off-white fill, black text) on Selector / Tertiary / Source Drawer Open — that's reserved for Primary/Secondary/Action Tapped.
  • Don't use #FFFFFF — the system's white is the cool-tinted Off-White #F1F3FC.
F.02 Foundations

Type is DIN Pro Medium, always.

One family, one weight, five scales. Hierarchy comes from size and tracking, never from weight contrast. Barlow Condensed is the sanctioned web fallback; JetBrains Mono is reserved for technical readouts (timestamps, IDs, system labels).

Do

  • Make every component consume type from a named style (Button/M, Header/H7, etc.) — the type style owns size, line-height, tracking and casing.
  • Always specify font-weight: 500 explicitly.
  • Preserve fractional values verbatim (line-height 104.762px, letter-spacing 2.161px).
  • Apply text-box trim on every number component — Figma uses Vertical Trim by default, CSS does not.

Don't

  • Don't introduce DIN Pro Regular / Bold / Light / Italic.
  • Don't override a type style's casing inline — if a Button/M-styled label renders lowercase, it's a bug.
  • Don't mix more than two type scales in a single composition.
  • Don't substitute fonts outside the documented fallback chain.

F.04 Foundations

Architectural sharpness, graduated radii.

The system uses a graduated radius scale, not a single value. Mixing rule: within a single composition, use at most two radius levels. Combining xs (5px) and 4xl (100px) on adjacent elements creates discord.

F.05 Foundations

Elevation via tonal layers and glass.

EMRC uses tonal stepping (Surface → Panel → Panel-Deep) and translucent overlays — not drop shadows. Drop shadows are reserved for one purpose: urgency on Primary / Action Highlight states.

The two structural moves

Tonal stepSurface → Panel → Deep
Panel · #0e131c
Panel-Deep · #0a0e14
Surface → Panel → Panel-Deep tonal sequence
Glass selected patternblur(20) + rgba(255,255,255,0.20)
Selected
The system Selected pattern — Selector, Tertiary (Tapped), Source Drawer (Open)

Shadow tokens

Primary Highlightbox-shadow: 0 4px 50px rgba(120, 122, 255, 0.5)
Action Highlight0 4px 50px rgba(120,122,255,0.55) + outer rings 0 0 0 12px rgba(120,122,255,0.08), 0 0 0 24px rgba(120,122,255,0.04)
Selected pattern (system)backdrop-filter: blur(20px) · rgba(241, 243, 252, 0.2) · 1px rgba(241, 243, 252, 0.3) border
Action Bar (Transparent)backdrop-filter: blur(50px) · rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3)
Graph Commentbackdrop-filter: blur(12px) · rgba(241, 243, 252, 0.1)

Do

  • Use box-shadow only for Primary/Action Highlight states — never as decoration.
  • Apply backdrop-filter via class-based stylesheets (not inline style props) — React can silently bail.
  • Place persistent chrome (Header, ChapterTree, Action Bar, Source Drawer Badge) at z-index ≥ 10.

Don't

  • Don't use drop shadows on cards, panels, buttons-at-rest, or text.
  • Don't invert color in the Selected pattern. Tint, never invert.
  • Don't assume DOM presence equals visual presence — z-stacking, opacity-at-scale and overflow clipping all hide elements that exist.
F.06 Foundations

The grid is 3840 × 2160. Always.

Eight landscape touchpoints render at 3840 × 2160 native; the Energy Dashboard at 2160 × 3840 portrait. All component dimensions in this system are literal pixel values at landscape reference. Smaller landscape surfaces (43", 40") scale the same DOM proportionally via transform: scale(). Inside the stage, every value MUST be a literal Figma pixel. No vw, no vh, no cqw, no approximations.

Touch ergonomics — the reach rule

65" displays were rejected at hardware spec because, at touch distance (50–80cm), users couldn't reach the top without blocking the view. All interactive controls must live in the bottom third of the screen.

Header zone · y 60–88px · read-only status
Hero content · y 88–1700 · frame-specific
Left clusterLanguage (FI · EN, both always visible) + Chapter Tree
CenterAction Bar
RightSource Drawer

Touch zone · y 1700–2160 · landscape 3840 × 2160 · exception: DC1/DC2 leaned-over tables (rule lifted) · Energy Dashboard portrait (rule rotates with frame)

Each component lives at a fixed x,y in the Figma source — overlap is a non-issue by construction. Treat the three sub-zones as semantic slots, not as flex regions.

C.00 Components · Header

Header — the persistent top row.

1611 × 28, sits at top: 60 with 88px offsets from the screen edges. Three clusters: LEFT carries LUT branding + live CO₂ readout (Fingrid), CENTER shows the current section indicator, RIGHT shows place + time. Always at z-index ≥ 10 — must sit above any content background.

Anatomy

LEFT cluster (JetBrains Mono 16, 3px tracking)LUT University · EMRC at 25% opacity  ·  2 × 20 vertical divider  ·  10 × 10 green dot, box-shadow: 0 0 12px rgba(74,222,128,0.533)  · NN gCO₂/kWh in #4ade80  · ↓ clean at 20% opacity
CENTER (DIN Pro 40, +8px tracking)Section indicator NN SECTIONNAME at 30% opacity — updates at Phase 4 of the chapter transition
RIGHT cluster (JetBrains Mono 16, 2px tracking)LAHTI at 20% opacity  ·  10.30 at 45% opacity
Color of CO₂ readoutBrand spine green rgb(74,222,128) when grid is clean (≤ 50 g) — flips to average/negative when grid dirties (TBD with designer)
PositioningAbsolute top: 60 · left: 88 · right: 88 · width 1611 inside that band

Do

  • Place the Header at z-index ≥ 10 so content backgrounds never cover it.
  • Update the section indicator only at Phase 4 of the chapter transition — it switches in lock-step with the ChapterTree's selected tag.
  • Render the time in JetBrains Mono with a dot separator (10.30) not a colon — system convention.
  • Drive the CO₂ value from Fingrid; poll cadence 60s.

Don't

  • Don't centre the Header — it lives inside left/right clusters, with the section indicator anchored to centre.
  • Don't recolor the green dot — it's the brand spine 'clean grid' signal.
  • Don't change the format of the CO₂ readout — always <code>NN gCO₂/kWh</code>.
  • Don't show the Header on Cover frames — Cover is its own composition.
C.01 Components · Buttons

Buttons — five variants, three states.

Primary, Secondary, Action, Tertiary, Icon. Each carries Default, Highlight and Tapped. Action is reserved for show-stopping CTAs in the main content area — never the bottom nav, with one documented exception (the Cover frame's START stack).

Buttons · all variants357:25613
Primary · Secondary
Action (150 tall)
Tertiary · Icon
1500 × 780 @ native
State applies to every variant on this canvas

Specs

PrimaryElectric fill · 100h · 100px radius · Button/M · padding 40/32 · gap 16
SecondaryTransparent · 1px Off-White border · 100h · 100px radius · matches Primary geometry
ActionElectric fill · 150h · 150px radius · Button/L · padding 56 · gap 24
TertiaryTransparent · 75h · 38px radius · Button/S · 1px rgba(241,243,252,0.3) border
Icon100 × 100 · 100px radius · holds a 32px chevron / plus glyph
HighlightAdds glow — Primary: 0 4px 50px rgba(120,122,255,0.5). Action stacks two outer rings.
TappedColor inversion — Off-White fill + Black text. Exception: Tertiary Tapped uses the Selected pattern, never inversion.

Do

  • Use Primary for the default narrative advance — one per frame.
  • Use Action sparingly — START, FIGHT!, RUN SIMULATION. Main content area only.
  • Switch to Highlight after 5 seconds of inaction, or when the action is urgent.

Don't

  • Don't put Action inside the bottom navigation. The Cover START stack is the only documented exception.
  • Don't lowercase a button label. Uppercase is baked into Button/M and Button/S type styles.
  • Don't invert color on Tertiary Tapped — use the Selected glass pattern.
  • Don't use Highlight as the resting state — it loses its meaning.

Do

  • Keep Selector labels UPPERCASE in both Default and Selected states.
  • Apply the system Selected pattern — blur(20) + 0.2 tint + 0.3 border.
  • Composite the Language selector to the LEFT of the Chapter Tree, in the bottom-left zone. The two ride together as one navigation cluster.
  • Render BOTH supported languages (FI · EN) in the Language pill at all times — one active, one muted at ~45% off-white. The pill is a state indicator, not a dropdown.

Don't

  • Don't invert color (Off-White fill + Black text) on the selected state.
  • Don't omit the border on Selected — the 0.3 hairline is part of the pattern.
  • Don't render Language labels lowercase — that's a type-style bypass, not a feature.
  • Don't mount the Language selector anywhere except adjacent-left of the Chapter Tree — that's the only declared position.
  • Don't hide the inactive language. The pill always shows FI · EN together — it's a swap, not a dropdown or a per-tap reveal.

Do

  • Show the numeric prefix only on the Selected tag.
  • Use Inactive (30% opacity, solid border) for chapters the visitor hasn't reached.

  • Don't show the Action Button on documentary, system or transition frames — it's a hook-only signal.
  • Don't change the centre label text on hook frames — always ABSTRACT.
  • Don't put the Action Bar on the left or right — it's always centred bottom.
C.04b Components · Bottom Nav

Bottom Nav — the touch zone, composed.

The bottom 460px of every landscape touchpoint (y 1700–2160) is one composed cluster, not three independent components. Left → right: Language pill (FI · EN, both always visible) + Chapter Tree ride together as the navigation pair; Action Bar sits centred (with an Action Button floating above on Cover / Battle hook frames); Source Drawer anchors the right edge. The three sub-zones are semantic slots — every component lives at a fixed x,y, never a flex region.

C.06 Components · Bar

Bar — Sources and Needs.

903 wide. Sources Bar uses a 64px source icon and Electric fill at full opacity. Needs Bar uses a 96px need icon and Off-White at 50% opacity — visually distinct, not just swapped colors. End-cap handle is always Off-White at full opacity, regardless of bar topic.

Bar · three states82:59178
SOLAR80 %
PEAK DEMAND62 %
903 wide
Static → Dynamic adds drag handle → Selected scales value text & handle

Do

  • Sources Bar — 64px icon · Electric fill at full opacity.
  • Needs Bar — 96px icon · Off-White at 50% opacity. Visually distinct, not a color swap.
  • End-cap handle is always Off-White at 100% — the handle marks the current value.
  • Maintain 10–12px clear vertical whitespace between text baseline and the top of the bar track.

Don't

  • Don't color the handle to match the fill — it destroys the value signal.
  • Don't compress vertical rhythm in the 77px block — looks cramped at 4K touch distance.
C.07 Components · Battle Elements

Battle Elements — Stats · Info · Result.

The signature head-to-head pattern. Four primitives compose one Battle frame: Battle Stats (a full circle, with only the INNER half visible — the outer half is clipped by the gauge canvas — and the E / L letter watermarked inside) · Battle Info (caption + body, centred below each gauge) · Battle Result (the large percentage that reveals at FIGHT commit) · and the composite Battle Outcome block (C.21) that stitches all three plus an optional headline. Fills start at the BOTTOM of the visible half and grow UP the inner curve toward the apex at TOP. Spatial grammar: Electric LEFT (fill travels bottom → right → top), Legacy RIGHT (fill travels bottom → left → top) — the two leading edges meet at the apex. 180° max, never 360°.

Anatomy

Battle StatsFull circle (cx=400, cy=400, r=340 in an 800×800 viewBox) clipped to its INNER half by the gauge frame — the outer half hangs off-canvas. Track: 24px stroke off-white 18%. Fill: 36px stroke side colour, round cap.
Visible halfElectro shows the RIGHT half of its circle (curve bulges toward the centre of the composition). Legacy shows the LEFT half. The two visible halves face each other across the head-to-head gap.
LetterE (electro) / L (legacy) — outlined glyph (WebkitTextStroke: 2px <side>, transparent fill, 40% opacity), 600px Brand. Positioned centred inside the visible half (75% / 25% x-offset), never spanning into the clipped half.
Spatial grammarElectric LEFT, Legacy RIGHT — non-negotiable. Both fills start at the BOTTOM (cx, cy+r) and animate toward the apex (cx, cy-r). Electro leading edge travels bottom → right → top (sweep=0). Legacy travels bottom → left → top (sweep=1). They meet at the apex — the head-to-head beat.
AnimationElectric fills first: 380ms delay, 1900ms easeOutExpo. Legacy follows: 1000ms delay, 1350ms easeOutExpo. The asymmetry is the argument.
Battle InfoCaption (50px H5, +9% tracking) + body (32px P2). Centred under each gauge, paired by side. Colour: side's stat colour on the H5, off-white-70 on body.
Battle ResultThe large percentage value (260px Number/L). Appears at end-state only — fades in 800ms after the arc settles. Same colour as its side.
Composes toBattle Outcome (C.21) — adds a headline above the two sides + a description below, used on Battle result frames as the dramatic verdict block.

Do

  • Treat the gauge as a full circle that the frame clips in half — the visible half always faces the centre of the composition.
  • Fill is a 180° arc starting at the BOTTOM of the visible half, growing UP the inner curve toward the apex at TOP.
  • Stagger arc animations: Electric 380ms / 1900ms easeOutExpo, Legacy 1000ms / 1350ms easeOutExpo.
  • Reveal the Battle Result percentage AFTER the arc has settled — 800ms fade-in on the value.
  • Render the E / L letter as an outlined glyph at 40% opacity, centred in the visible half — watermark, never foreground.

Don't

  • Don't use 360° as the gauge maximum — fill is 180° max.
  • Don't show fill arcs in the Start state — only the empty inner-half tracks until FIGHT commits.
  • Don't start the fill at the top or right — always at BOTTOM of the visible half.
  • Don't animate both arcs simultaneously — the lead is part of the argument.
  • Don't reverse spatial grammar — Electric's fill always travels bottom → right; Legacy's always travels bottom → left.

P1 · Clear · 1000ms · E1 · Gentle

Do

  • Animate color directly on a single text element via interpolated rgb — never overlap two colored spans.
  • Stack old/new digits in a single CSS grid cell so both share the same baseline-anchored slot throughout.
  • Begin the color shift 30% into the size animation, so the eye registers scale before color.
  • Bring chrome back in stages: Chapter Tree + Language Selector at Phase 2 (number lands), Action Bar at Phase 4 (hook headline renders) — never all-at-once.
  • On reset, fade Chapter Tree, Language Selector and Action Bar out together — leave the start frame in its clean cinematic state.
  • On Cover → 01, skip the digit-flip phase. Total drops to ~5s.

Don't

  • Don't overlap two colored spans for the color crossfade — they render at subtly different baselines and produce visible misalignment.
  • Don't switch a digit between position: absolute and position: relative during the animation — causes a layout jump.
  • Don't show all chrome at once when the new chapter resolves — staging is the cinematic move.
  • Don't invent a cubic-bezier curve and ship as authoritative. Use Figma prototype settings (E1=Gentle, E2=Slow) or named presets until designer confirms.

Anatomy · Content Block L

Frame chromeThe preview composes Content Block L inside a complete SYSTEM frame so the panel's spatial role is visible: Header (C.00) pinned to the top edge; Bottom Nav (C.04b — no Action Button) along the bottom 460px touch zone. Bottom Nav prevails — Content Block L stops at y=1700 so it never extends into the touch zone. Bottom Nav only fades in special cases (e.g. a single phase of the Chapter Transition sequence).
PositionLEFT edge of the frame — the "L" stands for Left, not Large. Right 2840px is reserved for hero imagery / battle visual + the bottom touch zone.
Outer container1000 × 2160 · pinned to left edge · the panel BACKGROUND (glass tint + blur) extends the full canvas height so it visually anchors the left edge top-to-bottom. The Bottom Nav (chrome, z-index 10) sits on top of the panel's bottom 460px — nav buttons + Language pill never get hidden by the panel.
Backgroundrgba(0,0,0,0.2) tint · backdrop-filter: blur(20px)
Inner content758 wide × 1316 tall · left: 110, top: 184 · all four blocks stop at y=1500 inside the panel · the panel's bottom 460px is BACKGROUND ONLY, reserved for Bottom Nav chrome to render on top.
Block 1 · Title0–220h · Header/H6 40px Electric "LEVEL 1" + 80px Off-White subtitle · gap: 16
Block 2 · Subhead + body280–490h · 50px H5 LEFT-aligned caption + 32px Body/P2 paragraph · gap: 32. Caption inherits the panel's left edge — never centred.
Block 3 · Battle Elements600–1030h · 3× Test Outcome blocks (icon + value + target) · gap: 56. Lives below Block 2 with 110px breathing room — the body paragraph never crowds the numbers.
Block 4 · Generation Mix1090–1386h · 754 wide · compressed "GENERATION MIX LIVE" header + 6 source-bar rows (Wind, Solar, Nuclear, Hydro, Fossil, Storage/H₂)
SlotsEvery block is independently visible-toggleable — drop any block for a sparser frame. Whichever blocks remain, the panel must still fit within the 1700px height boundary so Bottom Nav prevails.

Do

  • Place Content Block L on the LEFT edge of the frame — the hero/imagery zone always sits on its right.
  • Cap Content Block L at height 1700 — it ends where the bottom touch zone (y 1700–2160) begins. Bottom Nav prevails.
  • Use the default with all four blocks for SYSTEM frames; toggle individual block visibility on hook frames or sparser layouts.
  • Left-align the SUBHEADLINE caption in Block 2 — the panel's text always reads from the left edge.
  • Use Test Outcome accents (positive/average/negative) on Block 3 — color is the verdict.
  • Use Selected pattern colors throughout — Electric for level marker + values, Off-White for body, Legacy for fossil-only data.

Don't

  • Don't extend Content Block L into the bottom touch zone (y 1700–2160). Bottom Nav prevails — it only fades in special cases like within one phase of the Chapter Transition sequence.
  • Don't place Content Block L on the right — that's not what 'L' means.
  • Don't centre-align the SUBHEADLINE caption — Block 2 reads left-aligned, like the rest of the panel.
  • Don't drop the backdrop-filter — without the glass, the panel reads as a solid div over the hero, not a layered surface.
  • Don't add a drop shadow — the tonal step + blur do the depth work.
  • Don't run text past 758px wide inside the panel — the inner content area is fixed at 758, not 1000.
  • Don't use Test Outcome colors anywhere except Block 3's Battle Elements — they're semantic verdict tokens, not decoration.
C.16 Components · Imagery

Gradient Backgrounds — seven structured atmospheres.

The stage is Surface #161c26. Gradient Backgrounds layer on top as structured geometric tints — bars, chevrons, concentric rings (vertical or head-to-head), stripes — each carrying a different visual rhythm and (where applicable) the Electric / Legacy spatial grammar. The seven variants are not interchangeable: each is bound to a storytelling code (§P.01) and a frame role. Element counts are 7 for the strip-based variants (Bars, Chevrons, Stripes) and 5 or 6 for the arc-based variants (Battle Arcs, Rings) — the arc circles are large (diameter ≥ 2× canvas height) with centres off-canvas, so each visible band reads as a wide flat curve.

Gradient Backgrounds · seven variants68:7175 + Imagery/index.jsx
FIVE BATTLES SETTLE THE ENERGY TRANSITION.
Variant: Battle Arcs — The Battle Code background — 5 Electric arcs centred OFF-CANVAS at the LEFT (cx=−1800, cy=1080) + 5 Legacy arcs centred OFF-CANVAS at the RIGHT (cx=5640, cy=1080). Each diameter ≥ 2× canvas height — bands read as wide head-to-head curves. The two fans face each other but do NOT touch — a clear dark valley spans the centre of the frame, where the head-to-head spine breathes.

All seven at a glance

Vertical Barsbars
Right Chevronschevrons
Rings · Bottomrings_bottom
Rings · Toprings_top
Stripes · Topstripes_top
Stripes · Bottomstripes_bottom
Battle Arcsbattle_arcs

Anatomy

Bars7 vertical bars · LINEAR height growth · no gap · each bar fades light Electric (bottom) → dark (top) via per-bar linearGradient.
Chevrons7 ≫ chevrons · NO GAP · the chevron apex (the dagger) lands on the canvas mid-vertical line (y=1080). Alpha 0.40 (LEFT, denser) → 0.08 (RIGHT, fading).
Rings · B / T6 wide Electric ARCS · 360px stroke = 360px spacing (no gap) · radii 1700 → 3500px · circle centre OFF-CANVAS at (1920, 3560) (Bottom) or (1920, -1400) (Top). Outermost band reaches the far edge of the canvas (apex at y≈60 for Bottom / y≈2100 for Top).
Stripes · T / B7 horizontal Electric stripes · 308px tall each · no gap · alpha 0.32 (anchor end) → 0.05 (far end). "Top" anchors at the top of the canvas, "Bottom" at the bottom.
Battle Arcs5 Electric arcs from off-canvas LEFT + 5 Legacy arcs from off-canvas RIGHT. Circle centres at (-1800, 1080) and (5640, 1080). Radii 2000 → 3360px, 340px stroke = 340px spacing. Outermost bands STOP short of canvas centre — leaving a wide dark valley spanning the head-to-head axis.

Do

  • Use Gradient Backgrounds only on Surface — they layer on top of #161c26, not as standalone canvases.
  • Bind the variant to the storytelling code: Battle Arcs = Battle Code · Bars / Chevrons = Cinema · Rings / Stripes = Documentary.
  • Stack them BEHIND content with z-index 0 — content sits above, chrome sits above content.
  • Render at 4K native (3840 × 2160) — the geometric pattern depends on stride values that don't scale.
  • Keep element counts canonical: 7 for Bars / Chevrons / Stripes, 6 for Rings · Bottom / Top, 5 per side for Battle Arcs. The rhythm IS the system.

Don't

  • Don't add a third color. The palette is Electric, Legacy, and the Surface they sit on — full stop.
  • Don't change the element counts. Strip-based variants are 7; ring variants are 6 (single-axis) or 5 per side (head-to-head).
  • Don't let the Battle Arcs fans touch in the middle — the dark spine is the head-to-head axis.
  • Don't anchor Rings or Battle Arcs at the canvas edge. The circle centres sit OFF-CANVAS — only the outer band of each ring shows.
  • Don't reverse the Battle variant. Electric LEFT, Legacy RIGHT — non-negotiable.

Don't

Anatomy

Plot area2310 × 1665 · positioned at left: 1200, top: 183 inside a 3840 × 2160 frame. Curves, gridlines and axis labels all use the same coordinate space — a value of 0.10 lands exactly where the "10%" tick sits.
Title clusterLeft 184 / top 184 / width ~920 — H6 label + 80px headline + 32px body
Y axisJetBrains Mono 22px · 45% opacity · 12% tracking · each tick positioned at top: H * (1 - y), centred vertically with translateY(-50%). Unit suffix per variant: % · $/MWh · °C · etc.
X axisJetBrains Mono 22px · same style as Y · justify-between across the plot width. Unit suffix per variant: years · GW · %.
Curve6px stroke · Area fill at 18% (Legacy) / 22% (Electric)
Crossover14px Off-White dot + 32px outlined halo at 40% opacity — marks the inflection point (Area variant only)
Graph Comment200px radius pill · backdrop-blur 12 · rgba(241,243,252,0.1) · Flag-anchored, asymmetric padding
Variant · Area crossoverTwo series cross over time. The crossover IS the story — paint Electric last so it sits over the Legacy fill after the inflection.
Variant · Stacked areaSix series stacked to 100%. Renewables use Electric at ascending opacity (Hydro 0.25 → Storage 0.85); Fossil takes Legacy. Use for composition + time.
Variant · Ranked bars10 horizontal bars · 460px label column (Flag + country) · barTrack rounded 100 at 6% off-white · fill in Electric · inline value at end. Use for rank-by-metric.
Variant · Multi-lineUp to 4 series · line opacity descends with rank (1.0 → 0.35) · last-point Flag callouts on the right gutter (W + 24). Use for trajectories of peers.
Variant · Scatter / bubbleBubble area encodes a third dimension (annual TWh). Renewable kind = Electric fill / stroke; Firm = Off-white; Legacy = Legacy red. Use for cost-curve maps.

Do

  • Pick the variant by the question — composition (stacked area), rank (ranked bars), trajectories (multi-line), cost-curve (scatter), crossover moment (area).
  • Keep the Y-axis range bound to the data — default to 0–100% for shares, or zoom in (e.g. 40–100%) when the story is in the variance and the lower band is dead space.
  • Render the chart geometry from data, not from Figma. Charts are governed by EMRC-design.md §13 — Data-Driven Components.
  • Share one coordinate system between curves, gridlines and axis labels — the '10%' tick must sit where the data point 0.10 sits, always.
  • Keep Electric on TOP visually when it rises above Legacy after the crossover — paint Electric last so it sits over the Legacy area.
  • Mark the crossover with a dot + halo. It IS the story.
  • Anchor every Graph Comment with a Flag — flags are how the visitor reads the geography of the data.

Don't

  • Don't mix variants in one chart — a stacked-area-plus-scatter mashup loses both stories.
  • Don't let axis labels and curves drift out of sync — if the chart says 10% but the curve floats at the 40% line, the chart is lying.
  • Don't transcribe chart curves from Figma — they lose data semantics. Author the component in React with a runtime data prop.
  • Don't use Test Outcome colors on the curves — Electric / Legacy carry the semantic verdict.
  • Don't tile the axis labels in DIN Pro — JetBrains Mono is the technical-readout font.
  • Don't add a chart legend when the title cluster already enumerates the series — only Stacked Area needs an inline legend (six rows, named).
P.01 Patterns · Storytelling Codes

Four codes. One per frame.

Every frame uses exactly one storytelling code. Mixing codes in a single frame is forbidden.Each code specifies a compositional grammar — bilateral split, three-column input/mix/output, hero figure with sparse type, narrative-photo-with-mono-citation. These are not style suggestions; they're contracts.

CODE 01
Battle

Head-to-head comparison. Two protagonists in opposite corners. Full-circle gauges, only the inner half visible (outer half clipped by the canvas). Fills travel from BOTTOM up the inner curve to apex at TOP on FIGHT — the leading edges meet at the apex.

USED ON: BEV vs ICE · System Overview Battles · 'what's known vs what's needed' in RGN
CODE 02
Documentary
EMBER · Q3 2025 · 2,537 TWh
FIRST CROSSOVER SINCE 1919

Narrative photo + text. Cinematic still, supporting copy. Deep dark background, monospace numerics, green confirmation markers, sources visible.

USED ON: Introduction sequences · Last Frontier · transition pages between sections
CODE 03
Cinema
03

Immersive scenic moments. Hero figure dominant, sparse text, atmospheric. Type contrast is the move.

USED ON: Lumina · opening hooks · closing ripples
CODE 04
Builder
NOTE

Three-column input/mix/output. Input controls LEFT, mix configuration CENTRE, KPI feedback RIGHT (on #0a0e14 panel-deep). Sticky notes at right edge.

USED ON: System Overview Section 02 · future interactive frames
P.02 Patterns · Architecture

Two registers, one touchpoint.

Every System Overview touchpoint runs Register 1 (the sequenced narrative — 01 → 02 → 03 → 04 → 05) and Register 2 (the parallel Sources & Research evidence layer) at the same time. Register 1 is the default experience; Register 2 rewards depth-seekers. Visitors enter via the Source Drawer badge on any narrative frame; returning is always available.

Register 1 · Narrative flow
01 INTRODUCTION
02 SYSTEM
03 BATTLES
04 TRANSITION
05 LAST FRONTIER
5–7 pages per section, 30–50 words per page. Battle Code's two-panel copy (~25–35 words on screen, ~10s reading time) sets the density target.
Register 2 · Sources & Research
SOURCE 01
SOURCE 02
SOURCE 03
SOURCE 04
SOURCE 05
SOURCE 06
Netflix-style browse pattern. Cards tap-to-expand. No timers, no required order. Reading is visitor-paced.

Z-Stacking — a runtime footnote, not a design concern

Components don't overlap by design — every primitive has a fixed Figma x, y, and the three sub-zones in F.06 Layout are semantic slots, not flex regions. At runtime, persistent chrome (Header, Chapter Tree + Language pill, Action Bar, Source Drawer Badge) still gets z-index: 10 defensively so a Panel-Deep side panel appearing later in source order can never visually cover chrome rendered earlier. The frame draft author doesn't place chrome — the registry-mounted primitives place themselves. This footnote is here for debugging only: a Header span in the DOM but invisible on screen means someone broke the defensive z-stack.

P.03 Patterns · Builder Code

Builder — input · mix · output.

System Overview Section 02. Three-column layout — Electrification (consumer + industry loads, LEFT), Grid Mix (electricity sources, CENTRE), Grid Test (KPIs + interpretive comment cards, RIGHT). The right column sits on Panel-Deep (#0a0e14) so the output reads as visually separate from the inputs. Two canonical states from Figma: Baseline (frame 383:23650 — current LIVE state, static bars, "BUILD YOUR OWN GRID" CTA) and Full Re-engagement (frame383:23694 — interactive sliders, scenario / preset / environmental-variable button banks, "NEXT" CTA).

Anatomy

Frame3840 × 2160 · three columns of 1280 each · LEFT/CENTER on Surface, RIGHT on Panel-Deep (#0a0e14) to mark the output zone · column dividers as 1px hairlines.
Header zoney 0–180 — C.00 Header pinned at the top (section "02 SYSTEM").

LEFT · ElectrificationTitle (50px) + optional date (Baseline only) · two grouped sections: CONSUMER LOADS (EV PENETRATION, EBUSES, EVTOL, MICRO-MOBILITY) + INDUSTRY LOADS (HDV TRUCKS, DATA CENTERS, H₂ PLANTS). Full-RE adds EXAMPLE SCENARIOS button bank at the foot.
CENTER · Grid MixTitle with optional LIVE green accent · ELECTRICITY SOURCES section: WIND, SOLAR, NUCLEAR, HYDRO, FOSSIL (Legacy red value), STORAGE/H₂. Full-RE adds PRESETS button bank at the foot.
RIGHT · Grid TestTitle with optional LIVE green accent · 4 KPIs (EFFICIENCY, STABILITY, INTENSITY, EMISSIONS) — each KPI = eyebrow + icon glyph + value (60px Brand in Test Outcome color) + target + a colored Comment Card (10px radius, 1px Test Outcome border, 2-line interpretation). Full-RE adds ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES button bank at the foot.
Slider rowIcon (44px in 56×56 cell, off-white) · Label (24px Brand uppercase) · Track (6px, off-white-10) · Fill (Electric, Legacy for FOSSIL) · Value (24px Electric/Legacy). Full-RE adds a 28px Off-White handle ringed by 2px Surface + 1px Off-White-45 at the value position.
KPI blockEyebrow (20px JetBrains Mono, 55% off-white, +14% tracking) · Icon glyph + Value (64px Brand, Test Outcome color) · Target (18px JetBrains Mono, 45% off-white). Comment Card: 10px radius, 1px Test Outcome border, 20px headline (Test Outcome color) + 16px body (off-white-70).
Button bankCentred row · 64px tall pills · 10px radius · 1px 18% off-white border · first item active (selected glass: 18% off-white + blur(20) + 30% off-white border). Three banks: EXAMPLE SCENARIOS (LEFT, 4 items) · PRESETS (CENTER, 5 items) · ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES (RIGHT, 5 items).
Builder CTAReplaces the stepper inside the Action Bar. Electric pill, 100h × auto, 100px radius, Black 24px Button/L label + 28px arrow. Label: BUILD YOUR OWN GRID on Baseline · NEXT on Full-RE.

Do

  • Compose Builder as exactly three columns — Electrification (LEFT) · Grid Mix (CENTER) · Grid Test (RIGHT). The right column lives on Panel-Deep to mark the output zone.
  • Show LIVE accents on column titles in Baseline only — once the visitor enters Full-RE they are editing, not reading live data.
  • Place button banks (Example Scenarios · Presets · Environmental Variables) ONLY in Full-RE, centred at the foot of their respective column.
  • Reserve Test Outcome colors for KPI values + their Comment Card borders — that's the only place those colors live.
  • Always pair a KPI with a 2-line Comment Card — the value is the quantitative signal, the comment is the qualitative interpretation.
  • Replace the stepper inside the Action Bar with the Builder CTA pill — BUILD YOUR OWN GRID (Baseline) / NEXT (Full-RE).

Don't

  • Don't mix Builder Code with Battle, Documentary, or Cinema in the same frame.
  • Don't show sliders in Baseline — the bars are read-only readouts of the current state.
  • Don't show LIVE in Full-RE — once the visitor is editing, the readout is a scenario projection.
  • Don't put KPI on Surface — the tonal step to Panel-Deep is what marks 'output zone'.
  • Don't use Electric / Legacy on KPI values — Test Outcome accents are the only valid colour for measured results.
  • Don't omit the Comment Card — KPIs need qualitative interpretation, not just numbers.
  • Don't render the Builder CTA in any colour except Electric — it's the Builder's primary action.
R.01 Rules · Anti-patterns

The running list of don'ts.

Every mistake caught, recorded here. Adding to this list is a normal part of the process — it gets longer over time, not shorter.

Figma reading6 items
  • Calling get_design_context without first calling get_metadata.
  • Redrawing Figma's image assets as your own SVG approximations.
  • Approximating Figma pixel positions as percentage calc() expressions.
  • Reusing chrome code from a previous frame instead of reading fresh.
  • Writing HTML before showing the human the layout table.
  • Treating designer-given frame names ("Frame 5160") as node IDs.
Transcription5 items
  • Rounding fractional pixel values (4.5074px → 4.5px is wrong).
  • Simplifying calc() expressions that resolve to plain numbers.
  • Substituting fonts outside the documented fallback chain.
  • Omitting font-weight: 500 even when family name implies medium.
  • Hand-composing multi-piece icons from percentage insets — replace with single flat asset img.
Layout4 items
  • Placing result texts inside the gauge circles — they belong below, between the two stats.
  • Centring bottom descriptions — left desc is left, right desc is right.
  • Putting navigation at the top of landscape touchpoints.
  • Placing the Action Bar on the left or right.
Gauges5 items
  • Using 360° as the gauge max — half-circle is 180° max.
  • Starting the arc anywhere other than the BOTTOM of the visible half.
  • Bulging the fill into the clipped (outer) half — the fill must travel along the visible inner curve.
  • Showing filled arcs on the FIGHT frame before FIGHT! is pressed.
  • Animating both sides simultaneously — Electro leads by 380ms, Legacy follows after 1000ms.
Spatial grammar3 items
  • Placing Electro on the right or Thermal on the left.
  • Mixing Battle Code with Documentary Code in a single frame.
  • Using Electric on the right side or Legacy on the left.
Buttons & chrome4 items
  • Putting FIGHT! inside the Action Bar — Action floats above it.
  • Showing NEXT before the result frame is reached.
  • Changing the centre label text on hook frames (always ABSTRACT).
  • Lowercase buttons — always uppercase via Button/M type style.
Sources3 items
  • Hiding Sources & Research on long content frames.
  • Changing the (N) counter format.
  • Placing Sources on the left side.
Process4 items
  • Shipping a Mode 2 story without its Figma template — Promote is the gate.
  • Generating code from Figma screenshots alone — always read get_design_context.
  • Adding a new component without writing its Figma description first.
  • Dropping a landscape template into the portrait Energy Dashboard.
R.02 Rules · Using the system

How a new frame gets built.

Lane 2 stories build exclusively by filling existing page templates. There is no "compose-a-new-archetype from masters" path in the current OS. If a story needs a layout no template covers, the story is blocked at Signal until a template is authored.

The 6-step Figma reading discipline

STEP 01Get URL
Designer hands over a Figma URL. Extract fileKey + nodeId. Don't treat the frame name as a node ID.
STEP 02Read structure
Call Figma:get_metadata first — never go straight to get_design_context.
STEP 03Layout table
Build a verbatim layout table. STOP. Wait for human approval before any code.
STEP 04Read implementation
Now call get_design_context — assets, typography, every component description.
STEP 05Transcribe
Write HTML by verbatim transcription. 4.5074px stays 4.5074px. calc() expressions stay verbatim.
STEP 06Compare
Side-by-side with the Figma frame. Zero pixel differences is the bar. 'Close enough' is failure.

Three-layer component architecture

primitives/1:1 with Figma components, leaf-level. Consume only DESIGN.md tokens, HTML, basic React.
compositions/Arrangements of primitives. No new visual elements. If a composition needs a new primitive, draw it in Figma first.
screens/Full-screen narrative states (Hook, Conflict, Journey, Pivot, Ripple). One per Sanity-stored Story phase.

Token consumption — three forms, only one is correct

✓ <button className="bg-electric text-black rounded-4xl">
✗ <button style={{ background: '#787aff', color: '#000', borderRadius: 100 }}>
✗ <button className="bg-[#787aff]">
When DESIGN.md updates a token value, every component referencing it by name updates automatically. Components bypassing tokens with literal values silently drift.
